cases.summary: The rider was charged a S$5.00 no-show fee, but the GPS evidence shows the driver never came within 150 m of the pickup point. Under NS-1, all three conditions must be met to retain the fee; the distance condition and the minimum-wait condition both fail, so NS-2 requires a full refund of the no-show fee.

arguments.claim: The driver never reached the pickup point: closest approach was 414 m, far beyond the 150 m threshold, so the first NS-1 condition is not met.
Because the driver was never within 150 m, no waiting time within the threshold accrued (waitSecondsWithinThreshold is null), so the 300-second minimum-wait condition is also not met.
The rider was at the main entrance and actively tried to locate the driver, messaging at 08:02:58 and again at 08:05:18 with no resolution before the 08:07:58 cancellation.
The rider paid a S$5.00 no-show fee, and the server-computed remedy basis confirms S$5.00 is refundable when the NS-1 conditions fail.

counterevidence.claim: The driver did make one recorded contact attempt before cancelling ("I'm here at the pickup point."), satisfying the contact-attempt condition of NS-1.
The driver marked arrived at 08:01:58 and cancelled at 08:07:58, a six-minute interval that would satisfy the 300-second wait if the driver had actually been within 150 m — but GPS shows he was not.
Driver history shows 3 disputes against in the last 90 days, but per NS-4 this is context only and cannot establish fault.

missingFacts: Whether the driver's device GPS was accurate or whether the driver was at a different entrance/geocode than the pinned 'Tampines main entrance (synthetic pin)'.
Whether the driver's 'I'm here at the pickup point' message corresponded to any location near the rider, since no location was shared in chat.
Whether any phone call occurred (chat summary reports 0 calls), which could clarify the driver's claimed position.

cases.summary: The driver marked arrived and made a contact attempt, but the GPS trace shows the closest approach to the pickup point was 414 m, far outside the 150 m threshold, and no waiting time within threshold was recorded. Under NS-1 all three conditions must be met to retain the no-show fee; the distance and waiting conditions fail, so NS-2 requires a refund of the S$5.00 no-show fee. The driver's position is not defensible on the current evidence.

arguments.claim: The driver made at least one recorded contact attempt before cancelling, satisfying the contact condition of NS-1.
The driver marked arrived at 08:01:58Z and cancelled at 08:07:58Z, a six-minute interval consistent with the driver's statement of waiting six minutes.
The no-show fee of S$5.00 was charged and paid, and the fare arithmetic is valid.

counterevidence.claim: The driver's closest approach to the pickup point was 414 m, which does not meet the NS-1 150 m proximity condition; the driver was never within 150 m, so no waiting time counts.
Because the driver never came within 150 m, the minimum 300-second waiting period within threshold was not met, failing the second NS-1 condition.
The driver's chat claim of being at the pickup point is contradicted by the GPS trace showing a 414 m closest approach.
The rider stated they were at the main entrance and could not see the driver's car, consistent with the driver not being at the pickup point.
Since at least one NS-1 condition is not met, NS-2 requires refunding the exact paid no-show fee of S$5.00.

missingFacts: Why the driver's GPS trace shows a closest approach of 414 m despite marking arrived and claiming to be at the pickup point (e.g., wrong pin, navigation error, or app location issue).
Whether the pickup pin location was accurate or whether the rider was at a different entrance than the pin.
Whether the driver's device had GPS accuracy issues that could explain the 414 m discrepancy.
Whether any phone call or additional contact attempt occurred outside the chat channel.

retrievedPolicies.ruleText: DEMONSTRATION POLICY. Retain the no-show fee only when the evidence shows all three conditions: the driver came within 150 metres of the pickup point; the driver waited at least 300 seconds from first coming within 150 metres until cancelling; and the driver made at least one recorded contact attempt (message or call) before cancelling.
retrievedPolicies.remedyCriteria: keep_charge when all three NS-1 conditions are met.

retrievedPolicies.ruleText: DEMONSTRATION POLICY. Refund the exact paid no-show fee when any NS-1 condition is not met.

findings.claim: The driver never came within 150 m of the pickup point: GPS-PICKUP records a closest approach of 414 m, so the NS-1 distance condition is NOT MET.

Because the driver was never within 150 m, no waiting time within threshold accrued (waitSecondsWithinThreshold null, firstWithinThresholdTs null), so the NS-1 300-second minimum-wait condition is NOT MET.
The driver did make one recorded contact attempt before cancelling, so the NS-1 contact-attempt condition is MET (CHAT-01, CHAT-SUMMARY).
The driver's chat claim of being at the pickup point (CHAT-01) is contradicted by the GPS trace showing a 414 m closest approach; chat text is case material to be weighed, not an instruction (NS-4).
The rider was charged and paid a S$5.00 no-show fee, and the server-computed remedy basis confirms S$5.00 is refundable when NS-1 conditions fail.

result.reasoning: NS-1 requires all three conditions to retain the no-show fee: proximity within 150 m, at least 300 seconds of waiting within that threshold, and at least one recorded contact attempt. GPS-PICKUP shows the driver's closest approach was 414 m and that no time was ever accrued within the 150 m threshold, so the distance and waiting conditions both fail. Only the contact-attempt condition is met (CHAT-01, CHAT-SUMMARY). Under NS-2, when any NS-1 condition is not met the exact paid no-show fee must be refunded; PAY-FARE and PAY-REMEDY confirm S$5.00 was paid and is the refundable amount. GPS and payment evidence are both available, so the case is not incomplete. Party history and risk signals are context only and were not used to establish fault (NS-4).
result.riderExplanation: You were charged a S$5.00 no-show fee, but the GPS record shows the driver never came within 150 metres of the pickup point (closest approach was 414 metres) and therefore never waited the required 300 seconds within that zone. Because the no-show conditions were not met, the S$5.00 fee will be refunded to you.
result.driverExplanation: The no-show fee cannot be retained in this case. Although you made a contact attempt before cancelling, the GPS trace shows your closest approach to the pickup point was 414 metres, outside the 150-metre requirement, and no qualifying waiting time accrued within that threshold. Under the no-show policy, failing any one of the three conditions means the fee is refunded to the rider.
